# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.

A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The ticket is about the Fa app (flutter_app) freezing ~3s after launch on iOS. Acceptance criteria:

1. Repro attempt — can't really repro on device here.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

This is a Flutter app in `flutter_app/`. Let me explore the boot path.

Now let me understand what blocking IO happens on the main isolate before the first frame:

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.
3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

The fix per the acceptance criteria:
- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.
- AC3: Boot watchdog — if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

Design: Add a `BootWatchdog`/`BootSteps` class in `flutter_app/lib/boot/`. Something like:

```dart
/// Boot-step breadcrumbs + a first-frame watchdog (gh-1507).
final class BootSteps {
  static final BootSteps instance = BootSteps._();
  ...
  final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
  final _steps = <String>[]; // completed boot steps with durations
  String? _currentStep;
  void step(String name) { ... }
```

And a watchdog: `BootWatchdog.install({Duration threshold})` — called at the very start of main/run(); uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` or a `Timer.periodic` to check: if the first frame hasn't been scheduled by threshold, log a breadcrumb "boot first frame > Ns" with uptime and last completed boot step, and crashlytics.log. Continue logging? One-shot or periodic (every N sec until first frame)? A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

Also instrument the boot stages in `app_boot.dart` with `BootSteps.step('services')` etc. before/after each awaited stage.

Also AC2 says defer heavy init post-frame: `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` is the classic heavy main-isolate work (locale data initialization for every supported locale is pure Dart parsing — milliseconds each, maybe ~100-500ms total). Firebase init is async plugin channel. The store loads are small disk reads. The heaviest pre-frame work is arguably `setUpWasmRuntime` (compiling wasm modules). {"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The ticket is about the Fa app (flutter_app) freezing ~3s after launch on iOS. Acceptance criteria:

1. Repro attempt — can't really repro on device here.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

This is a Flutter app in `flutter_app/`. Let me explore the boot path.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The ticket is about the Fa app (flutter_app) freezing ~3s after launch on iOS. Acceptance criteria:

1. Repro attempt — can't really repro on device here.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

This is a Flutter app in `flutter_app/`. Let me explore the boot path.

Now let me understand what blocking IO happens on the main isolate before the first frame:

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.
3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

The fix per the acceptance criteria:
- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.
- AC3: Boot watchdog — if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

Design: Add a `BootWatchdog`/`BootSteps` class in `flutter_app/lib/boot/`. Something like:

```dart
/// Boot-step breadcrumbs + a first-frame watchdog (gh-1507).
final class BootSteps {
  static final BootSteps instance = BootSteps._();
  ...
  final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
  final _steps = <String>[]; // completed boot steps with durations
  String? _currentStep;
  void step(String name) { ... }
```

And a watchdog: `BootWatchdog.install({Duration threshold})` — called at the very start of main/run(); uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` or a `Timer.periodic` to check: if the first frame hasn't been scheduled by threshold, log a breadcrumb "boot first frame > Ns" with uptime and last completed boot step, and crashlytics.log. Continue logging? One-shot or periodic (every N sec until first frame)? A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

Also instrument the boot stages in `app_boot.dart` with `BootSteps.step('services')` etc. before/after each awaited stage.

Also AC2 says defer heavy init post-frame: `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` is the classic heavy main-isolate work (locale data initialization for every supported locale is pure Dart parsing — milliseconds each, maybe ~100-500ms total). Firebase init is async plugin channel. The store loads are small disk reads. The heaviest pre-frame work is arguably `setUpWasmRuntime` (compiling wasm modules). Deferring wasm runtime post-frame might be too invasive. The minimal targeted fix is AC3 (watchdog) plus step breadcrumbs, which is what the ticket explicitly asks to add. AC2's audit can be partly addressed: run `_loadIntlDateSymbols` concurrently/unawaited post-routes since DateFormat is only needed for derived session titles which are lazily computed? Risky. Better: keep audit notes in rca.md/response.md, implement watchdog + breadcrumbs as the code change, and make one safe deferral: move `_loadIntlDateSymbols` after `runApp` (it's awaited inside bootTelemetry before routes). Actually bootTelemetry is awaited before routes; the intl symbols could be loaded without awaiting it before runApp — fire-and-forget. That's a safe targeted improvement: `unawaited(_loadIntlDateSymbols())`. DateFormat usage at runtime would just use en_US default until loaded... initializeDateFormatting caches into a global — if DateFormat is called before initialization for a non-en locale, it throws. When is DateFormat called? "derived session titles" — in session UI after boot. Post-frame loading likely wins. But there's a race risk. Hmm. Let me check supported locales count.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.

A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

# gh-1507: [BUG] TestFlight: app freezes ~3s after launch (1.0.536/216, iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27) — boot-path main-isolate hang

## Description

## TestFlight feedback (raw: feedback.json, no crash log attached)

- **Report**: "Just freezed" — app uptime **3000 ms** at report time (freeze ~3s after launch, i.e. during boot)
- Build: **1.0.536 (216)** — 12 versions behind main (1.0.548); the TestFlight leg has been failing (#1472), so testers run stale builds
- Device: iPhone16,1 (iPhone 15 Pro), iOS 27.0.1, arm64e, Wi-Fi, disk 3.4 GB free of 114 GB, battery 40%

Not a crash (no .ips attached) — a **hang/freeze during startup**, i.e. main-isolate block or deadlock in the boot path.

## Suspects (boot path, first ~3s)

Boot-path main-isolate work to audit for blocking IO / unawaited deadlocks:
1. Session/keys restore (`SessionKeysStore`, folder model pin restore)
2. Memory index / Obsidian vault scan at boot
3. Messaging fabric watcher + unified-root migration (`~/.fah/messages`)
4. Any synchronous network call before first frame (provider catalog fetch — the 180s connect watchdog covers provider streams, NOT app boot fetches)
5. JS/widget engine warmup, on-device model init (gemma/webllm lazy?)

## Acceptance

1. Repro attempt on current main build (1.0.548+) — cold start on iOS device, watch for boot hang; if unreproducible on current build, state which change since 1.0.536 plausibly fixed it.
2. Boot-path audit: no blocking IO on the main isolate before first frame; every boot fetch has a timeout; heavy init deferred post-frame.
3. Add a boot watchdog: if first frame takes > N sec, log a diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step) so the next TestFlight feedback is actionable without guessing.

## Notes

- Raw feedback: `feedback.json` only (TestFlight screenshot feedback without sysdiagnose). Device owner = developer (istin2007@gmail.com), so a sysdiagnose / repro is obtainable on request.
- Unblocks together with the TestFlight leg fix (#1477, merged in #1482 — first green daily with it expected 2026-10-11 ~05:30Z).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.

A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).
