# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.

3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

```

And a watchdog: `BootWatchdog.install({Duration threshold})` — called at the very start of main/run(); uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` or a `Timer.periodic` to check: if the first frame hasn't been scheduled by threshold, log a breadcrumb "boot first frame > Ns" with uptime and last completed boot step, and crashlytics.log. Continue logging? One-shot or periodic (every N sec until first frame)? A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

Also instrument the boot stages in `app_boot.dart` with `BootSteps.step('services')` etc. before/after each awaited stage.

Also AC2 says defer heavy init post-frame: `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` is the classic heavy main-isolate work (locale data initialization for every supported locale is pure Dart parsing — milliseconds each, maybe ~100-500ms total). Firebase init is async plugin channel. The store loads are small disk reads. The heaviest pre-frame work is arguably `setUpWasmRuntime` (compiling wasm modules). Deferring wasm runtime post-frame might be too invasive. The minimal targeted fix is AC3 (watchdog) plus step breadcrumbs, which is what the ticket explicitly asks to add. AC2's audit can be partly addressed: run `_loadIntlDateSymbols` concurrently/unawaited post-routes since DateFormat is only needed for derived session titles which are lazily computed? Risky. Better: keep audit notes in rca.md/response.md, implement watchdog + breadcrumbs as the code change, and make one safe deferral: move `_loadIntlDateSymbols` after `runApp` (it's awaited inside bootTelemetry before routes). Actually bootTelemetry is awaited before routes; the intl symbols could be loaded without awaiting it before runApp — fire-and-forget. That's a safe targeted improvement: `unawaited(_loadIntlDateSymbols())`. DateFormat usage at runtime would just use en_US default until loaded... initializeDateFormatting caches into a global — if DateFormat is called before initialization for a non-en locale, it throws. {"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

Now let me understand what blocking IO happens on the main isolate before the first frame:

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.
3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

The fix per the acceptance criteria:
- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.
- AC3: Boot watchdog — if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

Design: Add a `BootWatchdog`/`BootSteps` class in `flutter_app/lib/boot/`. Something like:

```dart
/// Boot-step breadcrumbs + a first-frame watchdog (gh-1507).
final class BootSteps {
  static final BootSteps instance = BootSteps._();
  ...
  final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
  final _steps = <String>[]; // completed boot steps with durations
  String? _currentStep;
  void step(String name) { ... }
```

And a watchdog: `BootWatchdog.install({Duration threshold})` — called at the very start of main/run(); uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` or a `Timer.periodic` to check: if the first frame hasn't been scheduled by threshold, log a breadcrumb "boot first frame > Ns" with uptime and last completed boot step, and crashlytics.log. Continue logging? One-shot or periodic (every N sec until first frame)? A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

Also instrument the boot stages in `app_boot.dart` with `BootSteps.step('services')` etc. before/after each awaited stage.

Also AC2 says defer heavy init post-frame: `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` is the classic heavy main-isolate work (locale data initialization for every supported locale is pure Dart parsing — milliseconds each, maybe ~100-500ms total). Firebase init is async plugin channel. The store loads are small disk reads. The heaviest pre-frame work is arguably `setUpWasmRuntime` (compiling wasm modules). Deferring wasm runtime post-frame might be too invasive. The minimal targeted fix is AC3 (watchdog) plus step breadcrumbs, which is what the ticket explicitly asks to add. AC2's audit can be partly addressed: run `_loadIntlDateSymbols` concurrently/unawaited post-routes since DateFormat is only needed for derived session titles which are lazily computed? Risky. Better: keep audit notes in rca.md/response.md, implement watchdog + breadcrumbs as the code change, and make one safe deferral: move `_loadIntlDateSymbols` after `runApp` (it's awaited inside bootTelemetry before routes). Actually bootTelemetry is awaited before routes; the intl symbols could be loaded without awaiting it before runApp — fire-and-forget. That's a safe targeted improvement: `unawaited(_loadIntlDateSymbols())`. DateFormat usage at runtime would just use en_US default until loaded... initializeDateFormatting caches into a global — if DateFormat is called before initialization for a non-en locale, it throws. When is DateFormat called? "derived session titles" — in session UI after boot. Post-frame loading likely wins. But there's a race risk. Hmm. Let me check supported locales count.

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

Now let me understand what blocking IO happens on the main isolate before the first frame:

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.
3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

The fix per the acceptance criteria:
- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.
- AC3: Boot watchdog — if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

```dart

  static final BootSteps instance = BootSteps._();
  ...
  final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

Now let me understand what blocking IO happens on the main isolate before the first frame:

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.
3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

The fix per the acceptance criteria:
- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.
- AC3: Boot watchdog — if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

Design: Add a `BootWatchdog`/`BootSteps` class in `flutter_app/lib/boot/`. Something like:

```dart
/// Boot-step breadcrumbs + a first-frame watchdog (gh-1507).
final class BootSteps {
  static final BootSteps instance = BootSteps._();
  ...
  final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
  final _steps = <String>[]; // completed boot steps with durations
  String? _currentStep;
  void step(String name) { ... }
```

And a watchdog: `BootWatchdog.install({Duration threshold})` — called at the very start of main/run(); uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` or a `Timer.periodic` to check: if the first frame hasn't been scheduled by threshold, log a breadcrumb "boot first frame > Ns" with uptime and last completed boot step, and crashlytics.log. Continue logging? One-shot or periodic (every N sec until first frame)? A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

Also instrument the boot stages in `app_boot.dart` with `BootSteps.step('services')` etc. before/after each awaited stage.

Also AC2 says defer heavy init post-frame: `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` is the classic heavy main-isolate work (locale data initialization for every supported locale is pure Dart parsing — milliseconds each, maybe ~100-500ms total). Firebase init is async plugin channel. The store loads are small disk reads. The heaviest pre-frame work is arguably `setUpWasmRuntime` (compiling wasm modules). Deferring wasm runtime post-frame might be too invasive. The minimal targeted fix is AC3 (watchdog) plus step breadcrumbs, which is what the ticket explicitly asks to add. AC2's audit can be partly addressed: run `_loadIntlDateSymbols` concurrently/unawaited post-routes since DateFormat is only needed for derived session titles which are lazily computed? Risky. Better: keep audit notes in rca.md/response.md, implement watchdog + breadcrumbs as the code change, and make one safe deferral: move `_loadIntlDateSymbols` after `runApp` (it's awaited inside bootTelemetry before routes). Actually bootTelemetry is awaited before routes; the intl symbols could be loaded without awaiting it before runApp — fire-and-forget. That's a safe targeted improvement: `unawaited(_loadIntlDateSymbols())`. DateFormat usage at runtime would just use en_US default until loaded... initializeDateFormatting caches into a global — if DateFormat is called before initialization for a non-en locale, it throws. {"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

Now let me understand what blocking IO happens on the main isolate before the first frame:

1. `bootServices()` — Firebase init, wasm runtime (`setUpWasmRuntime` — compiles WASM modules! This is heavy), dotenv load. All awaited before runApp.
2. `loadBootStores(env)` — ~12 sequential store loads, each awaited on the main isolate. These are disk reads (file reads through sandbox env on iOS) — blocking IO on the main isolate before the first frame.
3. `bootTelemetry()` — `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` loops over ALL supported locales and awaits `initializeDateFormatting` for each — heavy main-isolate work synchronously before the first frame.

The fix per the acceptance criteria:
- AC2: Boot-path audit — no blocking IO before first frame; heavy init deferred post-frame.
- AC3: Boot watchdog — if first frame takes > N sec, log diagnostic breadcrumb (uptime, last completed boot step).

So the deliverable: add a boot step tracker (breadcrumb infrastructure), and a boot watchdog that fires if first frame exceeds N seconds, logging uptime + last completed boot step to AppLog and Crashlytics breadcrumbs. Also possibly defer heavy init (intl date symbols) post-frame.

Design: Add a `BootWatchdog`/`BootSteps` class in `flutter_app/lib/boot/`. Something like:

```dart
/// Boot-step breadcrumbs + a first-frame watchdog (gh-1507).
final class BootSteps {
  static final BootSteps instance = BootSteps._();
  ...
  final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
  final _steps = <String>[]; // completed boot steps with durations
  String? _currentStep;
  void step(String name) { ... }
```

And a watchdog: `BootWatchdog.install({Duration threshold})` — called at the very start of main/run(); uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` or a `Timer.periodic` to check: if the first frame hasn't been scheduled by threshold, log a breadcrumb "boot first frame > Ns" with uptime and last completed boot step, and crashlytics.log. Continue logging? One-shot or periodic (every N sec until first frame)? A reasonable design: one diagnostic line at the threshold, then repeat at doubling intervals or every 30s while no first frame.

Also instrument the boot stages in `app_boot.dart` with `BootSteps.step('services')` etc. before/after each awaited stage.

Also AC2 says defer heavy init post-frame: `_loadIntlDateSymbols()` is the classic heavy main-isolate work (locale data initialization for every supported locale is pure Dart parsing — milliseconds each, maybe ~100-500ms total). Firebase init is async plugin channel. The store loads are small disk reads. The heaviest pre-frame work is arguably `setUpWasmRuntime` (compiling wasm modules). Deferring wasm runtime post-frame might be too invasive. The minimal targeted fix is AC3 (watchdog) plus step breadcrumbs, which is what the ticket explicitly asks to add. AC2's audit can be partly addressed: run `_loadIntlDateSymbols` concurrently/unawaited post-routes since DateFormat is only needed for derived session titles which are lazily computed? Risky. Better: keep audit notes in rca.md/response.md, implement watchdog + breadcrumbs as the code change, and make one safe deferral: move `_loadIntlDateSymbols` after `runApp` (it's awaited inside bootTelemetry before routes). Actually bootTelemetry is awaited before routes; the intl symbols could be loaded without awaiting it before runApp — fire-and-forget. That's a safe targeted improvement: `unawaited(_loadIntlDateSymbols())`. DateFormat usage at runtime would just use en_US default until loaded... initializeDateFormatting caches into a global — if DateFormat is called before initialization for a non-en locale, it throws. {"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

Another flaw: `_defaultThresholdMs <= 0` disables install entirely — good kill switch.

Now instrument `app_boot.dart`. Add marks:
- In `run()`/`runWithEnv()`: after bootWindow → mark('window'); install watchdog; after bootServices → mark('services'); in _runStages: after env created mark('env'); after loadBootStores mark('storage'); after bootTelemetry mark('telemetry'); before routes mark... actually mark('routes-mounted') after routes returns. Note routes() calls runApp synchronously; first frame comes later.

In `loadBootStores`: per-store marks: 'storage:sessionKeys', 'storage:registry', 'storage:lastConnection', 'storage:theme', 'storage:onboarding', 'storage:themePacks', 'storage:mediaModels', 'storage:taskModels', 'storage:onDeviceConfig', 'storage:imagePreviews', 'storage:networkWallet', 'storage:networkMode'. Keep concise.

Watchdog install: needs widgets binding → after bootWindow(). But note tests call runWithEnv in a test binding; install() will schedule a real Timer of 4s in test runs — test ends before it fires; timer canceled at first frame... In widget tests, a pending Timer may keep... flutter_test doesn't complain about pending timers unless using fakeAsync & verifyTimers. But 4000ms real timer in a `test()` — the test completes, timer fires at 4s while other tests run → fires debugPrint breadcrumb spuriously, and could leak across tests. Risk: spurious '[fah] BOOT-WATCHDOG' prints in later tests and, worse, BootSteps.reset in tests → timer firing later referencing new state. It's just a log line, but noisy. Better: make install injectable/disable-able for tests: add a static `BootWatchdog? override` in FaAppBoot? Simpler: give FaAppBoot a `bootWatchdog` field (nullable, default const-constructed? can't const due to fields). Add to FaAppBoot constructor: `BootWatchdog? watchdog` — when null, run()/runWithEnv() create the default one. Tests can pass a watchdog with tiny threshold... but existing tests don't pass one, so they'd create real 4s timers.

Alternative: don't create the watchdog inside runWithEnv unless... hmm. Real behavior needed: production must install. Tests: the boot tests runWithEnv multiple times; each installs a 4s Timer. First frame: in these tests no runApp/frame happens → timer fires at 4s → debugPrint line. Only a log line, once per install. Acceptable? It prints during unrelated tests potentially. flutter_test fails tests only on uncaught exceptions, not stray prints. But a Timer firing after test zone teardown → "A Timer is still pending" error happens only with FakeAsync verify. Real timers firing post-test just run in the test runner's zone... could throw "Bad state: No element"? _fire just calls debugPrint — safe.

Still, cleaner: store the watchdog instance on FaAppBoot and expose it so tests can dispose; also `install()` checks binding initialized. Let me add `final BootWatchdog watchdog;` to FaAppBoot with a default, and tests can ignore. To keep noise down, I'll keep it simple: single static watchdog installed once per process (guarded by a static bool or the `_timer != null` check on a shared instance). Shared instance: `BootSteps` is already a static singleton; make `BootWatchdog.instance`? A static singleton installed once avoids duplicate timers across runWithEnv test calls. But tests may want fresh instances — they can construct their own for unit tests. Production path: FaAppBoot installs `BootWatchdog.installDefault()` once per process.

I'll add a static `BootWatchdog? _installed` in BootWatchdog: `static BootWatchdog get installed => _installed ??= BootWatchdog();` and `installDefault()` installs the singleton. That bounds it to one timer per process.

Edge: `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=0` → install() returns; but `_installed` would return a watchdog whose install never arms — subsequent installs no-op too since _timer stays null and install() re-checks. install() is idempotent via `if (_timer != null) return;` but when disabled, repeated install() calls re-check `_defaultThresholdMs <= 0` and return each time. Good.

Let me restructure slightly: make `BootWatchdog.install()` an instance method as written, and in app_boot use a process-wide singleton:

```dart
static final BootWatchdog _watchdog = BootWatchdog();
...
_bootWatchdog() => _watchdog.install();
```

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

In widget tests, a pending Timer may keep... flutter_test doesn't complain about pending timers unless using fakeAsync & verifyTimers. But 4000ms real timer in a `test()` — the test completes, timer fires at 4s while other tests run → fires debugPrint breadcrumb spuriously, and could leak across tests. Risk: spurious '[fah] BOOT-WATCHDOG' prints in later tests and, worse, BootSteps.reset in tests → timer firing later referencing new state. It's just a log line, but noisy. Better: make install injectable/disable-able for tests: add a static `BootWatchdog? override` in FaAppBoot? Simpler: give FaAppBoot a `bootWatchdog` field (nullable, default const-constructed? can't const due to fields). Add to FaAppBoot constructor: `BootWatchdog? watchdog` — when null, run()/runWithEnv() create the default one. Tests can pass a watchdog with tiny threshold... but existing tests don't pass one, so they'd create real 4s timers.

Alternative: don't create the watchdog inside runWithEnv unless... hmm. Real behavior needed: production must install. Tests: the boot tests runWithEnv multiple times; each installs a 4s Timer. First frame: in these tests no runApp/frame happens → timer fires at 4s → debugPrint line. Only a log line, once per install. Acceptable? It prints during unrelated tests potentially. flutter_test fails tests only on uncaught exceptions, not stray prints. But a Timer firing after test zone teardown → "A Timer is still pending" error happens only with FakeAsync verify. Real timers firing post-test just run in the test runner's zone... could throw "Bad state: No element"? _fire just calls debugPrint — safe.

Still, cleaner: store the watchdog instance on FaAppBoot and expose it so tests can dispose; also `install()` checks binding initialized. Let me add `final BootWatchdog watchdog;` to FaAppBoot with a default, and tests can ignore. To keep noise down, I'll keep it simple: single static watchdog installed once per process (guarded by a static bool or the `_timer != null` check on a shared instance). Shared instance: `BootSteps` is already a static singleton; make `BootWatchdog.instance`? A static singleton installed once avoids duplicate timers across runWithEnv test calls. But tests may want fresh instances — they can construct their own for unit tests. Production path: FaAppBoot installs `BootWatchdog.installDefault()` once per process.

I'll add a static `BootWatchdog? _installed` in BootWatchdog: `static BootWatchdog get installed => _installed ??= BootWatchdog();` and `installDefault()` installs the singleton. That bounds it to one timer per process.

Edge: `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS=0` → install() returns; but `_installed` would return a watchdog whose install never arms — subsequent installs no-op too since _timer stays null and install() re-checks. install() is idempotent via `if (_timer != null) return;` but when disabled, repeated install() calls re-check `_defaultThresholdMs <= 0` and return each time. Good.

Let me restructure slightly: make `BootWatchdog.install()` an instance method as written, and in app_boot use a process-wide singleton:

```dart
static final BootWatchdog _watchdog = BootWatchdog();
...
_bootWatchdog() => _watchdog.install();

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1507 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: TestFlight build 1.0.536 (216) froze ~3 s after launch on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27 — a main-isolate hang/freeze in the boot path (no crash log attached).

**Root cause**: Not conclusively determinable from the shipped artifact — the feedback is a screenshot-only report ("Just freezed", app uptime 3000 ms) with no sysdiagnose and no crash log, and the repo snapshot is a single squashed release commit (v1.0.548), so the 1.0.536 → 1.0.548 diff cannot be audited locally. The freeze signature (uptime ≈ 3 s, no crash) matches the known boot-risk surface: `FaAppBoot.run()` awaits the full window → services → storage → telemetry chain (Firebase init, WASM runtime compile, ~12 sequential persisted-store disk loads, intl symbols) **before `runApp`**, and the post-frame restore (`_BootstrapScreen._boot` → `AgentService.create` → `createOrResumeSession`) runs several more awaited main-isolate disk reads while the boot spinner is on screen — indistinguishable from "frozen" to a tester.

**Impact**: On a slow/cold iOS start (Keychain unlock, first disk touch after reboot, large session JSONL) the main isolate blocks for seconds before or around the first frame; the UI shows a static spinner and TestFlight records a freeze.

**Fix approach** (per the ticket's acceptance criteria):
1. *Repro/AC1*: cannot run an iOS device in this environment; the build-gap statement is included in `outputs/response.md`. The stale-build root (TestFlight leg failing, #1472/#1482) is called out.
2. *Audit/AC2*: audited the boot path (findings below). Pre-frame blocking IO is inherent to the staged `await` boot; the individual loads are small and already guarded where network is involved (skill seeding 5 s timeout, `restoreAccount` fire-and-forget, provider streams carry the 180 s connect watchdog). No unsafe deferral was made blindly — deferring store loads past `runApp` would change restore semantics.
3. *Watchdog/AC3* (the code fix): add `BootSteps` boot-step breadcrumbs through the whole boot path (window/services/storage/telemetry/routes + each persisted store + the post-frame restore) and a `BootWatchdog` that fires if the first frame does not land within a threshold (default 4 s, `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS` overridable), logging uptime + completed/current boot steps through the existing debugPrint tee (console + `logs/app.log` + Crashlytics breadcrumb). It re-fires every 30 s while the frame never lands, so the next TestFlight feedback carries the exact step where boot wedged.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh bug, not returned).
